title: Identifying Implicit Research Data References in Paper Citations

live_model.evidence: Sec. 4.2: 'GPT-4.1 series (GPT-4.1-nano, GPT-4.1-mini, and GPT-4.1) ... We set the temperature to 0.0'; responses constrained to Yes/No via Structured Outputs.

prompt.location: Appendix A: Figure 5 (system prompt), Figure 6 (user prompt Con + Cite), Figure 7 (user prompt Con + Cite + Bib)

claim.location: Table 1, row GPT-4.1-nano, Con + Cite columns (accuracy 0.757, F1 0.181)

data.source: 783 citation tags from 10 papers of the public GSAP-NER dataset (Otto et al., 2023); the authors' data-reference labels (191 positives) are not stated as released

notes: Preliminary experiment; GPT-4.1-nano is the weakest GPT model in the table (headline rows are GPT-5.2 and GPT-5-mini). Label availability is the soft gap.

resolution.plan: The 783 citation contexts come from the public GSAP-NER papers, but the authors' 191 implicit-data-reference labels are not released (no URL or availability statement in the paper), so F1 cannot be computed; re-annotating would not reproduce the paper's labels.
